decisions.cross_method_reconciliation: Moderate signal for outcome prognosis, but treatment and effect modification signals are weak and inconsistent across folds.

evidence_for: Consistent outcome signal in penalized main (support 5/15) and predictive forest (support 5/15) models

decisions.cross_method_reconciliation: Evidence aligns across predictive forests for confounding and R-learners/causal forests for effect modification.

evidence_for: Predictive forest support for treatment (7/15)
Predictive forest support for outcome (7/15)

Treatment support in predictive forest (7/15)

decisions.rationale: Consistent evidence for confounding, while evidence for effect modification is too weak to justify a modifier role.

summary: The reviewed candidates exhibit a high prevalence of dual roles (confounder and effect modifier), particularly systemic inflammation markers (NLR) and pathological markers (Napsin A, N-stage). Several symptomatic markers (myelosuppression, neurological symptoms) also demonstrate dual roles. Myocardial infarction and night sweats are identified as confounders without sufficient evidence for modification, while necrotic fluid acts as an effect modifier. Mucositis presence showed insufficient evidence across the required roles.
